## The finding

Epic 6202's story **S1 (`aa40-cbda`) is CLOSED, but its deliverable was not in effect.** The
gate-scratch volume existed, attached, raw and unmounted; gate scratch ran on the ROOT filesystem
-- precisely the silent fallback S1 exists to prevent.

```
pre-fix (SSM, read-only): nvme2n1 50G no FSTYPE/no MOUNTPOINT, serial vol06780b8557d1416b7
blkid -> no filesystem; no gate-scratch line in fstab; both markers ABSENT; df / -> 49G/60G (81%)
```

AWS confirmed the volume `in-use` at `/dev/sdg` with a matching NVMe serial, so the device was
unambiguous. It was simply never formatted or mounted: `user_data.sh` runs under cloud-init on
FIRST BOOT ONLY, and the volume was created by a later `terraform apply`. The script is correct;
it never ran. A gap in the delivery path, not a logic bug.

Both alarms were correctly in ALARM throughout, so this WAS detected. What was missing is that S1
closed on code correctness without any check that the volume entered service.

## Why remediation was not a simple mount

`user_data.sh:236-238` writes two markers to deliberately DIFFERENT filesystems:
`.gate-scratch-required` on ROOT (survives an unmount), `.gate-scratch-mounted` on the VOLUME.
Declaration present + proof absent makes gate admission REFUSE rather than repopulate on root;
here BOTH were absent, so admission read "no dedicated volume" and gates ran on root.
`/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` held LIVE working directories, so mounting over them would HIDE them
while stranding the bytes on root. The ordered procedure is `infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md`.

AC1-AC4 and AC6 are HOST actions, tagged `[non-codebase]`, discharged by an operator running that
runbook. The code deliverable is the runbook plus AC5/AC7's delivery-gap assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [non-codebase] The gate-scratch volume is formatted, in `/etc/fstab` by UUID, and mounted at
      `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`. Proven by `mountpoint -q` and `lsblk` showing the fstype.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — `mountpoint -q` true; `lsblk` shows nvme2n1 xfs 50G at /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch; fstab line `UUID=7ea719fd-f65c-4e8f-992c-d74410b5ea4c ... xfs defaults,nofail 0 2`; device resolved BY SERIAL (vol06780b8557d1416b7), which mattered — lsblk ordering changed across the reboot in-session.
- [x] [non-codebase] Both markers exist on their intended filesystems, created in the safe order, and
      `chmod 0700` is applied. Proven by `ls` plus confirming they are on different devices.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — both present, and verified as the PROPERTY not mere presence: `stat -c %d` gives 66307 for /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required (root) vs 66306 for gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted (volume) — genuinely different devices. Written proof-first.
- [x] [non-codebase] `rebar/host:gate_scratch_mounted` publishes 1 and `disk_used_percent` resumes publishing;
      both alarms return to OK. Proven from CloudWatch, not from the host alone.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — CloudWatch datapoints, not StateReason: gate_scratch_mounted=1.0; disk_used_percent for the mount resumed after zero datapoints; both alarms read OK. State values checked explicitly to distinguish OK from INSUFFICIENT_DATA, since this host's probe-truncation defect can make an alarm leave ALARM by going blind.
- [x] [non-codebase] The stranded copy under root is reclaimed and `df /` reflects it.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — `df /` 42G/70% -> 19G/32%, ~23 GiB returned; gate-scratch itself 2.1G of 50G (5%).
- [x] AC5 (the only NON-`[non-codebase]` criterion). Concrete edit target:
      **`scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py`** (new) with its offline oracle
      `tests/unit/test_assert_volumes_in_service_dcc3.py` (new). It joins the two halves nobody
      had joined -- terraform's `aws_volume_attachment` set against the host's mount table --
      and fails, naming the volume, when one is attached but not in service. Three outcomes, not two:
      `UNKNOWN` (host did not report the device) stays distinct from `NOT-IN-SERVICE` and also
      fails. Flipping gate_admission to refuse on a missing declaration is filed separately as
      `reportable-commutual-rooster` (`1064-8c4a-f399-41de`).
- [x] [non-codebase] The review-bot container is RECREATED after the host mount, and the mount is
      verified FROM INSIDE it. `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:305` binds `/var/lib/rebar` —
      the PARENT — and Docker binds default to `rprivate` propagation, so a mount created on the
      host underneath a running container does NOT appear inside it. Without this the bot keeps
      writing to the shadowed pre-mount directory while every host-side check reads healthy.
      Proven by `docker compose exec review-bot sh -c 'stat -c %D /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch;
      stat -c %D /var/lib/rebar'` returning TWO DIFFERENT device ids, and by
      `.gate-scratch-mounted` being visible inside the container.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — recreated per runbook §7 and verified FROM INSIDE: `docker exec compose-review-bot-1 df -h` shows /dev/nvme2n1 on /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch, and a write test lands on device 10302 (volume) not 10303 (root).
- [x] AC7 -- the delivery gap is closed as a CLASS, and ONE mechanism is CHOSEN rather than
      left as an either/or. **Chosen: the apply-time signal, not a post-boot reconciler.**
      Positive rationale, not elimination: a reconciler could safely auto-MOUNT an already
      formatted volume, but this one was RAW, and auto-`mkfs` on a volume that merely looks
      blank is how a restored backup is destroyed -- so that branch cannot cover the case that
      actually occurred, and a half-covering automation is worse than an honest check.
      **Invocation point, stated:** `scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py` is a MANDATORY
      post-apply step, invoked from `infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md` §10 after this
      remediation and after ANY future `terraform apply` that adds or replaces a volume.
      Operation-linked deliberately, rather than bound to one CI provider, which is what
      `project.portability` requires.
      **Why it is not ALSO wired into `terraform-drift.yml`**, as a checkable fact rather than
      an omission: that workflow assumes the `rebar-terraform-plan` OIDC role, which is
      `ReadOnlyAccess` + `kms:Decrypt` (`infra/terraform/iam.tf:178-191`). `ssm:SendCommand` is
      a WRITE action absent from `ReadOnlyAccess`, so that role cannot run the host probe at
      all. Granting it is an IAM widening with its own blast radius and needs its own ticket.
      A fix that only mounts this one volume by hand would leave the next to be found the same
      way -- by an alarm, days later.

## Verification

AC5/AC7: `pytest tests/unit/test_assert_volumes_in_service_dcc3.py` and
`python scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py --instance-id i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (must exit 0,
both volumes `in-service`). `[non-codebase]` criteria: on the host by `mountpoint -q`, `lsblk`,
`findmnt --verify`, `stat -c %d` on both markers (must report DIFFERENT devices), `df -h /`, and
`docker exec compose-review-bot-1 df -h /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`; from CloudWatch by
`get-metric-statistics` on `gate_scratch_mounted` (=1) and `disk_used_percent` (resumed), with
both alarms read as OK, not INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
